bug_semantics: TemplateContext.Reset() cleared output, global, culture, and source-file state but left the per-context CachedTemplates dictionary intact. IncludeFunction.Invoke() resolves an include through TemplateContext.GetOrCreateTemplate(); a cache hit returns the previously compiled Template without calling ITemplateLoader.Load(). An application that pools or reuses a TemplateContext across requests, users, or tenants can therefore prime an include under one authorization context and, after Reset(), expose that stale include content to a later context.
flaw_origin: Direct atomic commit 2e95889099c3ee5e7a4c0147b7355ecd309200af added the public safe-reuse boundary TemplateContext.Reset() but omitted CachedTemplates.Clear() even though the cache and cache-hit include path already existed in its immediate parent. The vulnerability begins with this Reset contract, not with the older intentional within-context include cache; the commit is neither a move, refactor, revert, merge, nor squash aggregate.
ai_marker: Absent on the BIC commit object. `git cat-file commit 2e95889099c3ee5e7a4c0147b7355ecd309200af` shows human author Alexandre Mutel <alexandre_mutel@live.com>, the same human committer, subject `Add TemplateContext.Reset`, and no trailers, Generated-with text, AI co-author, or bot identity.
evidence: Advisory identity and mechanism: https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-58jr-9c6g-55jq identifies CVE-2026-74791 and points to the repository advisory https://github.com/scriban/scriban/security/advisories/GHSA-x6m9-38vm-2xhf; the latter states affected <=6.6.0, patched 7.0.0, and documents the stale admin-only/guest-view include-cache path. In the assigned full-history clone, `git grep -n -e 'GetOrCreateTemplate' -e 'CachedTemplates.TryGetValue' -e 'TemplateLoader.Load' 6.6.0 -- src/Scriban/Functions/IncludeFunction.cs src/Scriban/TemplateContext.cs` shows IncludeFunction.cs:41 calling GetOrCreateTemplate, TemplateContext.cs:1251 testing CachedTemplates, and Load at 1264 only on a miss. BIC: `git show --format=fuller --patch 2e95889099c3ee5e7a4c0147b7355ecd309200af` shows a one-parent, one-file commit adding Reset and its safe-reuse documentation while clearing only outputs, globals, cultures, and source files. `git log -L 964,993:src/Scriban/TemplateContext.cs HEAD` follows that method back to exactly 2e95889099c3ee5e7a4c0147b7355ecd309200af; `git log --all --full-history -S'public virtual void Reset()' -- src/Scriban/TemplateContext.cs` returns only that commit. Direct parent verification: `git grep -n 'public virtual void Reset' a2fc52e704e9c929e166d3ab7046081dfa8ab1fa 2e95889099c3ee5e7a4c0147b7355ecd309200af -- src/Scriban/TemplateContext.cs` returns only the child at line 817, while `git grep -n -e 'CachedTemplates' -e 'GetOrCreateTemplate' a2fc52e704e9c929e166d3ab7046081dfa8ab1fa -- src/Scriban/TemplateContext.cs src/Scriban/Functions/IncludeFunction.cs` proves the parent already had the dictionary and cache-hit include path. Fix: `git show --format=fuller --patch 099cb0491df92fafda95acb8c731c60d765bf41a` adds CachedTemplates.Clear() to Reset plus ResetShouldClearCachedTemplates, which switches loader content from admin-only to guest-view and expects the second render to reload. Tag boundary: `git grep -n 'public virtual void Reset' 3.8.2 3.9.0 -- src/Scriban/TemplateContext.cs` returns only 3.9.0, establishing the first vulnerable release after the BIC; `git grep -n 'CachedTemplates.Clear()' 6.6.0 7.0.0 -- src/Scriban/TemplateContext.cs` returns only 7.0.0. `git rev-parse 3.8.2^{commit} 3.9.0^{commit} 6.6.0^{commit} 7.0.0^{commit}` resolves respectively to 53da5bc08964319be948638f2747f8610b305e3c, 3d7c4e29e4803511cafe3724147276c2d60f7f9a, b5ac4bf30459fdc76964e3f751e16f7e96079ea7, and 25d148a104dd4d679a1a1932442616599e003c2f; `git tag --contains 099cb0491df92fafda95acb8c731c60d765bf41a --sort=version:refname` begins at 7.0.0.
reasoning: The older cache is intentional for repeated includes within one context; there was no Reset transition to violate. The smallest commit that created the advisory's cross-reuse condition is therefore the atomic addition of Reset with an explicit safe-reuse promise and incomplete state clearing. Its immediate parent has the cache machinery but no Reset method, so the vulnerable lifecycle is absent there; 3.9.0 is the first tag containing the BIC. The direct repair clears the cache and is first released in 7.0.0, matching the repository advisory's <=6.6.0/7.0.0 boundary. The BIC commit object is human-authored and contains no AI attribution. Although the later repair commit has a Copilot co-author trailer, protocol requires judging AI solely from the BIC, so AI involvement in the fix cannot change the NOT_AI verdict.
